signatures.docstring:
Extract analytic context fields that situate the outcome data within the correct test arm and study design, including the linked index test, unit of analysis, sequence of tests, and time interval between tests.

Form Questions:
- linked_index_test: "What is the label of the index-test arm to which this outcome row belongs?"
- unit_of_analysis: "Is the 2×2 table counting patients or lesions?"
  Options: Patient, Lesion
- sequence_of_tests: "In what order were the index test(s) and reference standard performed?"
- time_interval_rs_it: "What was the time interval between the index test and the reference standard (biopsy)?"

These fields establish the analytic framework needed to correctly interpret and link 2×2 outcome data to the appropriate test arm and study design context.

input_fields.desc: Full markdown content of the diagnostic accuracy study paper from which analytic context fields are to be extracted.
input_fields.name: markdown_content

output_fields.name: linked_index_test
hints: Look for the index test name or label in the Methods section, typically under 'Index Tests', 'Study Arms', or 'Interventions'
In multi-arm studies, identify the specific arm label used consistently throughout the paper
The label should match exactly what was recorded in the Index Test form for this study
rules: Copy the label verbatim as it appears in the paper, preserving capitalisation and punctuation
Must exactly match the index_test_arm_label used in the Index Test form
For single-arm studies, use the sole index test name
Use "NR" if the index test label cannot be determined
output_fields.description: Label of the index-test arm to which this outcome row belongs — must exactly match the index_test_arm_label in the Index Test form (e.g., 'Vital Staining (1% Toluidine Blue)'). Required for multi-arm studies to correctly link outcome rows to test arms.

output_fields.name: unit_of_analysis
hints: Check the Methods section under 'Study Population', 'Participants', or 'Statistical Analysis' for whether the unit is patients or lesions
Look for phrases like 'per patient', 'per lesion', 'lesion-level analysis', or 'patient-level analysis'
If the paper reports multiple lesions per patient and analyses them individually, select 'Lesion'
rules: Must be exactly one of: 'Patient' or 'Lesion'
Use exact spelling and capitalisation as listed in options
Use "NR" if the unit of analysis cannot be determined from the paper
output_fields.description: Whether the 2×2 table counts patients or lesions. Studies enrolling one lesion per patient use 'Patient'; studies enrolling multiple lesions per patient use 'Lesion'. This determines which N fields are relevant.

output_fields.name: sequence_of_tests
hints: Look in the Methods section under 'Study Procedures', 'Protocol', or 'Data Collection'
Check for phrases describing the order of examination, staining, and biopsy
In vital-staining studies, staining (index test) typically precedes biopsy (reference standard) — confirm this from the text
rules: Describe the sequence clearly, naming both the index test and reference standard
For multi-test studies, list all tests in the order they were performed
Quote or closely paraphrase the paper's description of the procedure sequence
Use "NR" if the sequence is not reported
output_fields.description: Order in which the index test(s) and reference standard were performed (e.g., 'Index test before reference standard', 'Reference test before index test'). For multi-test studies list all tests in order. Quote or paraphrase from the paper.

output_fields.name: time_interval_rs_it
hints: Look in the Methods section under 'Study Procedures', 'Protocol', or 'Biopsy'
Check for phrases like 'immediately after', 'same session', 'same day', or specific time durations between staining and biopsy
In vital-staining studies, the biopsy is often performed in the same clinical session immediately after staining
rules: Report the time interval as stated in the paper, including units (e.g., minutes, hours, days)
If the biopsy was performed immediately after the index test in the same session, state this explicitly (e.g., 'Same session — biopsy performed immediately after staining')
Use "NR" if the time interval is not reported
output_fields.description: Time interval between the index test and the reference standard (biopsy). In most vital-staining studies the biopsy is performed on the same day immediately after staining — note this if evident. Use NR if not reported.

signatures.docstring:
Extract counts of patients and lesions who received only one of the two tests (index test or reference standard) to assess missing-data asymmetry in a diagnostic accuracy study.

Form Questions:
- n_patients_rs_not_it: "How many patients received the reference standard (biopsy) but NOT the index test?"
- n_patients_it_not_rs: "How many patients received the index test but NOT the reference standard?"
- n_lesions_it_not_rs: "How many lesions received the index test but NOT the reference standard (lesion-level studies only)?"
- n_lesions_rs_not_it: "How many lesions received the reference standard but NOT the index test (lesion-level studies only)?"

These fields capture one-sided test receipt to evaluate differential verification bias and missing-data patterns. The unit_of_analysis context field indicates whether the study analyses patients or lesions, which determines whether lesion-level fields are applicable.

input_fields.desc: Full markdown content of the diagnostic accuracy research paper to extract from
input_fields.name: markdown_content

input_fields.desc: Previously extracted unit_of_analysis with source grounding from another signature (contains 'value' and 'source_text' keys), indicating whether the study analyses patients or lesions
input_fields.name: unit_of_analysis

output_fields.name: n_patients_rs_not_it
hints: Look in the flow diagram, participant flow section, CONSORT/STARD diagram descriptions, or methods section for counts of patients who underwent biopsy but not the index test
Check footnotes or exclusion tables that describe why some biopsied patients lacked index test results
May appear as a discrepancy between total biopsied patients and total patients with index test results
rules: Report the integer count as a string value
Report '0' if the paper explicitly states none were missing
Report 'assumed 0' if the paper implies all biopsied patients also received the index test but does not state it explicitly
Report 'NR (probably N)' if the number can be estimated from context, replacing N with the estimate
Use 'NR' if the count is entirely unknown and cannot be estimated
Do not confuse with patients excluded before any testing
output_fields.description: Number of patients who received the reference standard (biopsy) but NOT the index test, used to assess missing-data asymmetry.

output_fields.name: n_patients_it_not_rs
hints: Look in the flow diagram, participant flow section, or methods/results for counts of patients who had the index test but did not proceed to biopsy
Check for descriptions of patients with negative index test results who were not biopsied, or patients lost before biopsy
May appear as a discrepancy between total index-tested patients and total biopsied patients
rules: Report the integer count as a string value
Report '0' if the paper explicitly states none were missing
Report 'assumed 0' if implied but not explicitly stated
Report an estimate with a note if the number can be inferred from context
Use 'NR' if the count is entirely unknown
Do not confuse with patients excluded before any testing
output_fields.description: Number of patients who received the index test but NOT the reference standard, used to assess differential verification bias.

output_fields.name: n_lesions_it_not_rs
hints: Only relevant when unit_of_analysis indicates lesion-level analysis
Look in the methods, results, or flow diagram for lesion-level counts describing lesions detected by the index test but not confirmed by biopsy or reference standard
May appear in tables comparing index test lesion counts to histopathology lesion counts
rules: Report the integer count as a string value
Use 'NR' if not reported or if the unit of analysis is patients rather than lesions
Report '0' if the paper explicitly states no lesions were missing reference standard verification
Report 'assumed 0' if implied but not explicitly stated
output_fields.description: Number of lesions that received the index test but not the reference standard, applicable only in lesion-level analysis studies.

output_fields.name: n_lesions_rs_not_it
hints: Only relevant when unit_of_analysis indicates lesion-level analysis
Look in the methods, results, or flow diagram for lesion-level counts describing lesions confirmed by biopsy or reference standard but not evaluated by the index test
May appear in tables comparing histopathology lesion counts to index test lesion counts
rules: Report the integer count as a string value
Use 'NR' if not reported or if the unit of analysis is patients rather than lesions
Report '0' if the paper explicitly states no lesions were missing index test evaluation
Report 'assumed 0' if implied but not explicitly stated
output_fields.description: Number of lesions that received the reference standard but not the index test, applicable only in lesion-level analysis studies.

signatures.docstring:
Extract diagnostic accuracy data (2×2 contingency table counts and derived statistics) from a diagnostic test accuracy study, using previously extracted index test and unit of analysis as context.

Form Questions:
- outcome_target_condition: "What is the exact outcome/target condition definition used to classify disease-positive and disease-negative in the 2×2 table?"
- tp: "How many true positives (index test positive AND reference standard positive) are reported?"
- fp: "How many false positives (index test positive BUT reference standard negative) are reported?"
- fn: "How many false negatives (index test negative BUT reference standard positive) are reported?"
- tn: "How many true negatives (index test negative AND reference standard negative) are reported?"
- reported_sensitivity: "What sensitivity (%) did the authors report?"
- reported_sensitivity_ci: "What is the 95% confidence interval for reported sensitivity?"
- reported_specificity: "What specificity (%) did the authors report?"
- reported_specificity_ci: "What is the 95% confidence interval for reported specificity?"
- reported_prevalence: "What is the prevalence of the target condition in the study population?"

These fields capture the core diagnostic accuracy data needed for meta-analysis. The linked_index_test and unit_of_analysis context fields identify which test and counting unit (patient vs. lesion) the 2×2 table refers to.

input_fields.desc: Full markdown content of the diagnostic accuracy study from which data are to be extracted
input_fields.name: markdown_content

input_fields.desc: Previously extracted index test with source grounding from another signature (contains 'value' and 'source_text' keys); used to identify which test's 2×2 table to extract
input_fields.name: linked_index_test

input_fields.desc: Previously extracted unit of analysis (e.g., patient-level or lesion-level) with source grounding from another signature (contains 'value' and 'source_text' keys); used to correctly interpret cell counts in the 2×2 table
input_fields.name: unit_of_analysis

output_fields.name: outcome_target_condition
hints: Look in the Methods section under 'Outcome', 'Reference Standard', 'Histopathology', or 'Diagnosis' subsections
The definition often appears near the description of the reference standard or biopsy classification
Copy verbatim if the paper states the classification explicitly
rules: State both the disease-positive category (e.g., 'dysplasia, carcinoma in situ and squamous cell carcinoma') and the disease-negative category (e.g., 'hyperplasia, inflammation and normal mucosa')
Copy verbatim from the document when clearly stated
Use "NR" if the target condition definition is not reported

examples.value: Disease positive are dysplasia, carcinoma in situ and squamous cell carcinoma. Disease negative are hyperplasia, inflammation and normal mucosa

output_fields.description: Exact outcome definition used to classify disease-positive and disease-negative in the 2×2 table, stating what is considered positive and what is considered negative.

output_fields.name: tp
hints: Look for a 2×2 contingency table, confusion matrix, or cross-tabulation in the Results section
May be labelled 'TP', 'true positive', or derivable from sensitivity × number of disease-positive cases
Check tables, figures, or supplementary material for cell counts
rules: Extract the integer count of true positives directly from the reported 2×2 table
Do not calculate from sensitivity/specificity unless the paper explicitly derives the count
Value must be a non-negative integer
Use "NR" if the 2×2 cell counts are not reported
output_fields.description: True positives: patients (or lesions) who tested positive on the index test AND had the target condition confirmed by the reference standard.

output_fields.name: fp
hints: Look for a 2×2 contingency table or confusion matrix in the Results section
May be labelled 'FP', 'false positive', or derivable from (1 − specificity) × number of disease-negative cases
Check tables, figures, or supplementary material for cell counts
rules: Extract the integer count of false positives directly from the reported 2×2 table
Do not calculate from specificity unless the paper explicitly derives the count
Value must be a non-negative integer
Use "NR" if the 2×2 cell counts are not reported
output_fields.description: False positives: patients (or lesions) who tested positive on the index test but did NOT have the target condition on biopsy.

output_fields.name: fn
hints: Look for a 2×2 contingency table or confusion matrix in the Results section
May be labelled 'FN', 'false negative', or derivable from (1 − sensitivity) × number of disease-positive cases
Check tables, figures, or supplementary material for cell counts
rules: Extract the integer count of false negatives directly from the reported 2×2 table
Do not calculate from sensitivity unless the paper explicitly derives the count
Value must be a non-negative integer
Use "NR" if the 2×2 cell counts are not reported
output_fields.description: False negatives: patients (or lesions) who tested negative on the index test but DID have the target condition on biopsy.

output_fields.name: tn
hints: Look for a 2×2 contingency table or confusion matrix in the Results section
May be labelled 'TN', 'true negative', or derivable from specificity × number of disease-negative cases
Check tables, figures, or supplementary material for cell counts
rules: Extract the integer count of true negatives directly from the reported 2×2 table
Do not calculate from specificity unless the paper explicitly derives the count
Value must be a non-negative integer
Use "NR" if the 2×2 cell counts are not reported
output_fields.description: True negatives: patients (or lesions) who tested negative on the index test AND did not have the target condition on biopsy.

output_fields.name: reported_sensitivity
hints: Look in the Results section, abstract, or summary tables for sensitivity values
May be labelled 'sensitivity', 'true positive rate', or 'recall'
If reported as a proportion (e.g., 0.9286), convert to percentage by multiplying by 100
rules: Express as a numeric percentage value without the '%' symbol (e.g., 92.86 not '92.86%')
Do not append a '%' symbol
Use a float if the reported value has decimal places
Use "NR" if sensitivity is not reported
output_fields.description: Sensitivity as reported by the study authors, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 92.86 means 92.86%).

output_fields.name: reported_sensitivity_ci
hints: Look adjacent to the reported sensitivity value for a confidence interval in parentheses or brackets
Check footnotes or supplementary tables if not in the main text
rules: Format as 'lower–upper' using an en-dash (e.g., '85.10–97.20')
Express bounds as percentages without '%' symbol
Use "NR" if the confidence interval is not reported
output_fields.description: 95% confidence interval for reported sensitivity, formatted as 'lower–upper' (e.g., '85.10–97.20').

output_fields.name: reported_specificity
hints: Look in the Results section, abstract, or summary tables for specificity values
May be labelled 'specificity', 'true negative rate', or '1 − false positive rate'
If reported as a proportion (e.g., 0.4545), convert to percentage by multiplying by 100
rules: Express as a numeric percentage value without the '%' symbol (e.g., 45.45 not '45.45%')
Do not append a '%' symbol
Use a float if the reported value has decimal places
Use "NR" if specificity is not reported
output_fields.description: Specificity as reported by the study authors, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 45.45 means 45.45%).

output_fields.name: reported_specificity_ci
hints: Look adjacent to the reported specificity value for a confidence interval in parentheses or brackets
Check footnotes or supplementary tables if not in the main text
rules: Format as 'lower–upper' using an en-dash (e.g., '30.10–61.20')
Express bounds as percentages without '%' symbol
Use "NR" if the confidence interval is not reported
output_fields.description: 95% confidence interval for reported specificity, formatted as 'lower–upper' (e.g., '30.10–61.20').

output_fields.name: reported_prevalence
hints: Look in the Results or Participants section for the proportion or percentage of participants with the target condition
May be derivable from the 2×2 table as (TP + FN) / (TP + FP + FN + TN)
For multi-arm papers, report study-level prevalence; if arm-level prevalences are given separately, list all
If OPMD and OSCC prevalences are reported separately, include both alongside the combined estimate
rules: Report as a descriptive string that may include multiple estimates (e.g., 'Oral cancer and OPMD - 51.7%; Oral cancer - 6.5%; OPMD - 45.2%')
Include the raw counts in parentheses if available (e.g., '83.6% (56/67)')
For multi-arm papers, prefix each estimate with the arm label (e.g., 'TB: 83.6% (56/67); AA: 73.5% (61/83)')
Use "NR" if prevalence cannot be reported or derived
output_fields.description: Prevalence of the target condition in the study population as reported or derivable from the data, which may include multiple estimates if the paper reports prevalence for OPMD and OSCC separately.

signatures.docstring:
Record reviewer annotations, general study-level notes, and the data source for an extracted outcome row in a systematic review.

Form Questions:
- comments_outcomes: "What reviewer notes apply to this outcome row (e.g., study arm assignment, dual-threshold issues, patient overlap between arms, meta-analysis notes)?"
- general_notes: "What additional free-text notes at the study or arm level are not captured elsewhere (e.g., methodological concerns, reviewer consensus, threshold anomalies, data-source clarifications)?"
- data_source: "What is the origin of this extracted data row (e.g., newly extracted for this review or sourced from a prior review dataset)?"

This signature depends on previously extracted TP, FP, FN, and TN values to provide context for the reviewer annotations.

input_fields.desc: Full markdown content of the systematic review document or data extraction form to extract reviewer notes and source information from.
input_fields.name: markdown_content

input_fields.desc: Previously extracted true positive count with source grounding from another signature (contains 'value' and 'source_text' keys).
input_fields.name: tp

input_fields.desc: Previously extracted false positive count with source grounding from another signature (contains 'value' and 'source_text' keys).
input_fields.name: fp

input_fields.desc: Previously extracted false negative count with source grounding from another signature (contains 'value' and 'source_text' keys).
input_fields.name: fn

input_fields.desc: Previously extracted true negative count with source grounding from another signature (contains 'value' and 'source_text' keys).
input_fields.name: tn

output_fields.name: comments_outcomes
hints: Look for inline reviewer annotations, footnotes, or comment fields associated with the specific outcome row
Check for notes about patient overlap, arm assignment, or meta-analysis flags near the TP/FP/FN/TN values
rules: Extract the reviewer's verbatim comment or annotation for this outcome row
Use "NA" (not "NR") when the reviewer explicitly indicates no notes are needed or when no comment field is present
Use "NR" only if the comments field is entirely absent from the document with no indication either way
Do not conflate outcome-row comments with general study-level notes

examples.value: There might be overlap of patients in different arms.

output_fields.description: Reviewer notes about this outcome row — e.g., which study arm the data belong to, dual-threshold issues, overlap between arms, or notes for meta-analysis. Use NA if no notes are needed.

output_fields.name: general_notes
hints: Look for a dedicated 'General Notes', 'Study Notes', or 'Reviewer Notes' section separate from per-outcome comments
Check for consensus statements, threshold comparison remarks, or methodological caveats at the study or arm level
rules: Extract the full free-text note verbatim as written by the reviewer
Use "NA" (not "NR") when the reviewer explicitly indicates no additional notes are needed
Use "NR" only if the general notes field is entirely absent from the document
Do not include outcome-row-specific comments here; those belong in comments_outcomes

examples.value: Reference Standard: Mild dysplasia is considered - no dysplasia in this case which is different from other study thresholds.

output_fields.description: Any additional free-text notes at the study or arm level not captured by other fields — methodological concerns, reviewer consensus notes (e.g., 'Carolina and Tanya reached a consensus'), threshold anomalies compared to other studies, or data-source clarifications. Use NA if no notes.

output_fields.name: data_source
hints: Look for a 'Data Source', 'Source', or 'Extracted by' label near the outcome row or at the top of the extraction form
Check for references to prior review names (e.g., author surnames like 'Walsh' or 'Lingen') or institutional labels (e.g., 'Upenn')
rules: Extract the data source label or description verbatim as it appears in the document
If the source is a prior review, include the reviewer/study name as written
Use "NR" if the data source is not reported or cannot be determined
output_fields.description: Origin of the extracted data row — whether it was newly extracted for this review or sourced from a prior review dataset (e.g., 'New data extracted by Upenn', 'Walsh', 'Lingen').
